'''Oleg Vladimirovich Deripaska''' ({{langx|ru|Олег Владимирович Дерипаска}}; born 2 January 1968)<ref name="Сайт Олега Дерипаска">{{cite web|url=http://www.deripaska.ru|title=Oleg Vladimirovich Deripaska|publisher=deripaska.ru|language=ru|access-date=7 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160208151706/http://www.deripaska.ru/|archive-date=8 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> is a [[Russian oligarchs|Russian oligarch]] and billionaire.<ref>[https://www.ft.com/content/08f230b0-4dfb-11e8-8a8e-22951a2d8493 Oleg Deripaska, Russian oligarch under siege for Putin ties], ''Financial Times'', 4 May 2018.</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/01/us/politics/deripaska-ohr-steele-fbi.html U.S. Agents Tried To Turn Oligarch Into an Informer] - New York Times, 1 September 2018.</ref> Deripaska began his career as a metals trader after the breakup of the [[Soviet Union]]. He used accumulated funds from trading to acquire stakes in the [[Sayanogorsk]] aluminium smelter from a consortium of businessmen who [[Privatization in Russia|privatized it in the aftermath of the collapse of the Soviet Union]].<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=2009-08-26 |title=Вещий Олег: биография Дерипаски |url=https://www.forbes.ru/ekonomika/lyudi/7207-veshchii-oleg-biografiya-deripaski |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=Forbes.ru |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Palma |first=Stefania |date=19 October 2021 |title=FBI searches home linked to Russian metals tycoon Oleg Deripaska |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/3af52cea-1710-4175-b236-0bebc9b51e26 |access-date=28 February 2022}}</ref> The Sayanogorsk aluminium smelter served as the foundation of what later became the world's largest aluminium company [[Rusal]].<ref name=":14" />

Deripaska is the founder of [[Basic Element (company)|Basic Element]], one of Russia's largest industrial groups, and Volnoe Delo, Russia's largest charitable foundation. He was the president of [[En+ Group]], a Russian energy company, and headed [[Rusal|United Company Rusal]], the second-largest aluminium company in the world, until he quit both roles in 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Devitt |first=Polina |last2=Lyrchikova |first2=Anastasia |date=February 19, 2018 |title=Russian magnate Deripaska to quit roles at his two biggest firms |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-rusal-deripaska/russian-magnate-deripaska-to-quit-roles-at-his-two-biggest-firms-idUSKCN1G31D3 |access-date=14 August 2018 |work=U.S. |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rusal.ru/en/about/management/|title=Management|publisher=[[Rusal|United Company Rusal]]|access-date=2 June 2017|archive-date=8 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160208151709/http://www.rusal.ru/en/about/management/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He has been characterized as a victor in the "aluminium wars" in Russia during the 1990s, which were frequently violent conflicts between businesspeople to obtain state-owned assets.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Devitt |first=Polina |last2=Lyrchikova |first2=Anastasia |last3=Golubkova |first3=Katya |date=21 December 2018 |title=Biting the bullet, not the dust: Deripaska gives up his aluminum empire |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-russia-sanctions-deripaska-rusal-idUSKCN1OK081 |access-date=28 February 2022 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Webb |first=Tim |date=13 April 2008 |title=The war of the four oligarchs |url=http://www.theguardian.com/business/2008/apr/13/mining.russia1 |access-date=28 February 2022 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref> In 2000, Deripaska founded Rusal, the result of a partnership between Sibirsky Aluminium and [[Roman Abramovich]]'s [[Millhouse Capital]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB106443818395367800|title=Aluminum Shake-Up May Loom in Russia|last=Whalen|first=Jeanne|date=25 September 2003|work=Wall Street Journal|access-date=2 June 2017|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> In 2007, Rusal merged with [[SUAL Group]] and [[Glencore]] International AG to form UC Rusal, with Deripaska as chairman.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/aluminium-russia-merger-idUSL2713534620070327|title=RUSAL, SUAL, Glencore complete aluminium merger|date=27 March 2007|work=[[Reuters]]|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref>
 
He was once [[List of Russian billionaires|Russia's richest man]], but lost a substantial part of his fortune during the [[2008 financial crisis]]. As of July 2025, his wealth was estimated by ''[[Forbes]]'' at $4.1 billion, making him the 887th richest person in the world.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=Oleg Deripaska |url=https://www.forbes.com/nft-profile/oleg-deripaska/ |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> In 2017, Deripaska obtained a [[Cypriot citizenship]] through the country's 'golden visa' program, which allows major investors in the economy to apply for a national passport.<ref name="guardian02032018"/>

He was placed under U.S. sanctions in 2022 for reasons relating to the 2014 annexation of Crimea by Russia.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-05-25 |title=Oleg Deripaska resigns from Rusal amid US sanctions row |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-44249933 |access-date=2022-03-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Treasury Designates Russian Oligarchs, Officials, and Entities in Response to Worldwide Malign Activity |url=https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sm0338 |access-date=2022-03-26 |website=U.S. Department of the Treasury |language=en}}</ref> Deripaska was one of [[List of people sanctioned during the Russo-Ukrainian War|seven oligarchs]] sanctioned by the British government over the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], including asset freezes and travel bans.<ref name="BBC_2022-03-10">{{cite web|date=10 March 2022 |title=Ukraine war: Roman Abramovich sanctioned by UK |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-60690362 |access-date=10 March 2022 |work=BBC News}}</ref>

As early as 2022, Deripaska was one of a handful Russian businessmen to openly denounce the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. After making his statements, he faced pressure from the Kremlin, leading to the seizure of a major asset he owned, valued at USD 1 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Billionaire Oleg Deripaska's Sochi hotel complex seized after Russian court order |url=https://www.ft.com/content/32052a11-89f3-4642-8dd4-11433a32f8a2 |date=19 December 2022 |website=www.ft.com}}</ref> Nonetheless, he returned to the subject in early August 2024, when he characterized the invasion as "madness" and called for it to be stopped immediately.<ref name="mt1">{{cite news |url=https://www.moscowtimes.ru/2024/08/08/milliarder-deripaska-nazval-voinu-putina-v-ukraine-bezumiem-i-prizval-nemedlenno-ee-ostanovit-a138992 |title=Миллиардер Дерипаска назвал безумной войну Путина в Украине и призвал немедленно ее остановить }}</ref> He came under strong fire from the pro-Putin camp in Russia for his statements, notably from the ultranationalist [[Aleksandr Dugin|Alexander Dugin]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-09 |title=Russia's Deripaska under fire for rare anti-war comments |url=https://uk.news.yahoo.com/russias-deripaska-under-fire-rare-145138943.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAEeWMalASYTRFnk0akqTeJk3JKEoMwdUL3sgzVv4XPIHyaHY08gSfeOYoFIwARMF5YrX5eENMPZXTzWKGCEQ5Iiqr2fqjpjlv_Y3wwMtvtbttrxSHXMX6_lAynmwEgqJ0_pPyFSG-tBMkVe0OqnMpJ-cdaqU1JD4c1Y4p_mZmkmd |access-date=2024-08-16 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Deripaska was born to a Jewish family in [[Dzerzhinsk, Russia|Dzerzhinsk]], [[Nizhny Novgorod Oblast]], [[Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic|Soviet Russia]] and grew up in [[Ust-Labinsk]], [[Krasnodar Krai]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=Russian oligarch tied to Putin charged with violating US sanctions {{!}} The Times of Israel | url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/russian-oligarch-tied-to-putin-charged-with-violating-us-sanctions/amp/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929205456/https://www.timesofisrael.com/russian-oligarch-tied-to-putin-charged-with-violating-us-sanctions/amp/ | access-date=2026-08-18 | archive-date=2022-09-29}}</ref> His parents came from [[Kuban]].<ref>{{cite news|script-title=ru:Олигарх Дерипаска участвовал в приеме парада Кубанского казачьего войска|url=https://yasnonews.ru/news/politika/oligarkh_deripaska_uchastvoval_v_prieme_parada_kubanskogo_kazachego_voyska/|access-date=25 May 2017|work=Yasno|date=22 April 2017|language=ru|archive-date=6 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606100753/https://yasnonews.ru/news/politika/oligarkh_deripaska_uchastvoval_v_prieme_parada_kubanskogo_kazachego_voyska/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Deripaska grew up on the family's small farm, where from the age of 5 or 6, he learned how to live off the land from his grandparents,<ref name=":0">{{cite news|title=Deripaska Rebound From Near-Crash Stares Down Potanin|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2011-02-21/deripaska-rebounding-from-near-disaster-stares-down-potanin-as-metals-soar|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|access-date=13 January 2016|first=Stephanie|last=Baker|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|date=22 February 2011}}</ref> who primarily raised him after his widowed mother, an engineer, had to leave to find work.<ref name="globeandmail2011">{{cite news|last1=Reguly|first1=Eric|title=At home with Russian oligarch Oleg Deripaska|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/careers/careers-leadership/at-home-with-russian-oligarch-oleg-deripaska/article573998/?page=all|access-date=25 May 2017|work=The Globe and Mail|date=11 February 2011|language=en-ca}}</ref> Deripaska credits his grandparents for teaching him the discipline of hard work along with farming.<ref name=":0" /> Both his grandfathers fought in the [[Second World War]]. His maternal grandfather returned to Russia after the war ended.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|title=PROFILE: 'We're waiting for the aluminium industry to do its homework,' Deripaska says |url=http://www.metalbulletin.com/Article/3250360/Search/PROFILE-Were-waiting-for-the-aluminium-industry-to-do-its.html?PageId=196010&Keywords=deripaska&OrderType=1&PageMove=2#axzz3sPgcUxAJ |publisher=metalbulletin.com |access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> His paternal grandfather Timofey Deripaska (1918-1945) – an ethnic Ukrainian – <ref name="memorial1">{{Cite web|url=https://pamyat-naroda.ru/heroes/memorial-chelovek_prikaz75047118/|title=Дерепаско Тимофей Романович: Приказ об исключении из списков|website=Память народа 1941—1945}}</ref> was killed in battle and buried in a mass grave in [[Austria]] — in his memory, Deripaska built a [[Russian Orthodox]] church in the town [[Laa an der Thaya]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazeta.ru/social/news/2019/05/09/n_12957151.shtml|title=Русский храм в австрийском городе Лаа провёл службу в память жертв Второй мировой войне - Газета.Ru &#124; Новости|website=Газета.Ru|date=9 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rns.online/r/6q5r/|title=В Австрии прошла служба в память о погибших советских солдатах|date=9 May 2019|website=Информационное агентство RNS}}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref><ref>[https://iz.ru/876646/2019-05-09/sluzhba-v-pamiat-o-sovetskikh-voinakh-proshla-v-russkom-khrame-v-avstrii Служба в память о советских воинах прошла в русском храме в Австрии]</ref>

Deripaska's first job was at the Ust-Labinsk plant where his mother worked. At age 11, he became an electrician's apprentice doing maintenance on electrical motors.<ref name=":1" /> His talent for math allowed him to enroll at the physics faculty of Moscow State University in 1985.<ref name=":0" /> One year into his studies, he was conscripted into the armed forces and served in the Soviet [[Strategic Missile Forces]]<ref name=":0" /> in the [[Transbaikal Military District|Trans-Baikal district]] of Siberia from 1986 to 1989.<ref name=":1" />

In 1993, Deripaska graduated with honors in physics from [[Moscow State University]];<ref>{{cite web|title=Basic Element – History|url=http://www.basel.ru/en/history/|access-date=28 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923182539/http://www.basel.ru/en/history/|archive-date=23 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> however, the [[Dissolution of the Soviet Union|collapse of the Soviet Union]] greatly reduced academic funding, making it impossible for him to continue his studies as a [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]].<ref name=":1" /> There were no available stipends or grants for students. "We had no money. It was an urgent and practical question every day. How do I earn money to buy food and keep studying?" he recalls.<ref name=":1" /> In 1996, he earned a master's degree from the [[Plekhanov Russian University of Economics|Plekhanov University of Economics]].<ref name="globeandmail2011"/>

== Career==
At the age of 25, teaming up with fellow physicists, engineers and rocket scientists, Deripaska set up his first metal trading company, VTK. He adopted a systematic, scientific approach to [[commodity trading]]. "I represented companies that were buying and selling raw materials", Deripaska said.<ref name=":0" /> Deripaska undertook export [[arbitrage]], buying metal at low Russian prices and selling it abroad at significantly higher international market prices. Deripaska traded primarily through the Baltic state of [[Estonia]], as the Russian system of export licenses was in disarray.<ref name=":0" /> "I started my business at an unusual moment in history. The country in which I was born and raised had disappeared, although the new country was not fully formed. The first one gave me an excellent education; the second one gave me the chance of success", Deripaska recalled in an interview with ''[[Metal Bulletin]]''.<ref name=":1" />

He used nearly all his arbitrage and trading profits to acquire his initial package of shares in the [[Sayanogorsk]] aluminium smelter in [[Southern Siberia]].<ref name="FACTBOX: Who is Oleg Deripaska">{{Cite news|title=FACTBOX: Who is Oleg Deripaska?|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-deripaska-profile-idUSTRE51L1IH20090222|work=[[Reuters]]|date=22 February 2009|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref>

In 1994, Deripaska became director general of the plant at the age of 26.<ref name=":0" /> In 1997, he founded Sibirsky (Siberian) Aluminium Group, which in 2000 merged with [[Roman Abramovich]]'s [[Millhouse Capital]] to create RUSAL.<ref>{{Cite web|title=RUSAL battle set for British court|url=http://www.stabroeknews.com/2012/news/world/07/07/rusal-battle-set-for-british-court-2/|work=Stabroek News|date=7 July 2012|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> In 2003, businesses led by Deripaska increased their stake in those companies under common management to 75% by acquiring half of the interest managed by Millhouse Capital.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB955986247819859000|title=Russia's Aluminum Barons Form Cartel to Control 10% of Output|author=Jeanne Whalen|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|access-date=14 January 2016|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> In 2004, the consolidation of RUSAL's ownership by companies related to Deripaska was completed with the acquisition of the remaining 25% equity interest in RUSAL managed by Millhouse Capital.<ref name=":6">{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB106443818395367800|title=Aluminum Shake-Up May Loom in Russia|author=Jeanne Whalen|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|access-date=14 January 2016|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Deripaska was named businessman of the year in 1999, 2006, and 2007 by ''[[Vedomosti]]'', a Russian business daily.{{citation needed|date=February 2024}}

[[RUSAL]] went on to become the largest aluminium producer in the world, until the [[China Hongqiao Group]] surpassed it in 2015. In 2010, under Deripaska's leadership, Rusal became the first Russian company to be listed on the [[Hong Kong Stock Exchange]].<ref name=":1" />

===Basic Element===
Beyond metals, which as of 2016 remained at the core of his diversified industrial holding, Deripaska has acquired stakes in a wide range of companies in various sectors, including energy, manufacturing, commercial vehicles, auto components, financial and insurance services,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sberbank of Russia: Basic Element, Sberbank and Changi Airports International sign Memorandum of Understanding for Airport Business Partnership|url=http://data.sberbank.ru/en/press_center/all/index.php?id114=11014378|website=data.sberbank.ru|access-date=13 January 2016|archive-date=20 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320162109/http://data.sberbank.ru/en/press_center/all/index.php?id114=11014378|url-status=dead}}</ref> leasing businesses, construction,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Строительство|url=http://www.basel.ru/building-realty/Construction/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150318192513/http://www.basel.ru/building-realty/construction/|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 March 2015|website=basel.ru|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> aviation, and agriculture. Among his assets are a Siberian power company {{ill|EuroSibEnergo|ru|ЕвроСибЭнерго}},<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurosib.ru/eng/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090511060730/http://www.eurosib.ru/eng/ |url-status=dead |title=EuroSibEnergo company website|archive-date=11 May 2009}}</ref> that is Russia's biggest private energy company; he owns 10% of [[Ingosstrakh]], one of Russia's largest insurance companies; [[GAZ Group]], a producer of cars, trucks and buses, founder of agricultural business (Kuban Agro Holding).<ref name=":3">{{cite web|url=http://www.ahkuban.ru|title=Agroholding Kuban website|publisher=ahkuban.ru|access-date=7 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160213030222/http://www.ahkuban.ru/|archive-date=13 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Агрохолдинг "Кубань" и производитель семян Maisadour создают СП в России|url=https://www.vedomosti.ru/business/articles/2015/11/30/618839-kuban-maisadour-sp|website=www.vedomosti.ru|access-date=13 January 2016|date=30 November 2015}}</ref> He established a transport company to run airports in the [[Krasnodar Krai|Krasnodar region]], including [[Sochi]] and Krasnodar.<ref name=":4">{{cite web|url=http://www.basel.aero/|title=Basel Aero website|publisher=basel.aero|access-date=7 November 2012|archive-date=18 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118225209/http://basel.aero/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

All these assets form part of the diversified investment and industrial group Basic Element.<ref name=":5">{{cite web|url=http://www.basel.ru/en/regions|title=Basic Element website|date=1 January 2008|publisher=Basel.ru|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723091302/http://www.basel.ru/en/regions/|archive-date=23 July 2011|url-status=dead|access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref>
Deripaska is the founder of [[Basic Element (company)|Basic Element]], a diversified investment group established in 1997 which has been managing investments in the following sectors: [[Energy (society)|energy]], metals and mining, machinery, [[financial services]], agriculture, construction, and aviation. The major investments under Basic Element management included stakes in [[United Company RUSAL]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rusal.ru/en/Default.aspx|title=RUSAL company website|publisher=Rusal.ru|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110409195407/http://www.rusal.ru/en/Default.aspx|archive-date=9 April 2011|url-status=dead|access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref> (the world's largest aluminium and alumina producer), [[GAZ Group]] (an [[Automotive industry|automotive company]]), [[Aviakor|Aviakor aircraft manufacturer]], EuroSibEnergo (ЕвроСибЭнерго (an [[energy supply]] company)<ref name=":2" /> Glavmosstroy (Главмосстрой) (a construction company)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.glavmosstroy.ru/eindex.htm|title=Glavmosstroy website|publisher=Glavmosstroy.ru|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110907045059/http://www.glavmosstroy.ru/eindex.htm|archive-date=7 September 2011|url-status=dead|access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref> Kuban Agroholding (an agricultural company)<ref name=":3" /> and Basel Aero (an aviation business comprising the three largest airports in the Krasnodar territory, and a joint venture with Changi Airports International).<ref name=":4" /> Basic Element has been managing Deripaska's investments into companies in Russia, the [[Commonwealth of Independent States|CIS]] countries, Africa, Australia, Asia, Europe and Latin America, which employ as many as 250,000 people.<ref name=":5" /> Strikeforce Mining and Resources (SMR) is also controlled by Basic Element.<ref name=finfor>{{Cite web|url=https://fin-forex.com/bazel-has-refused-to-purchase-copper-combine-in-serbia|archive-url=https://archive.today/20091102092826/http://fin-forex.com/bazel-has-refused-to-purchase-copper-combine-in-serbia/ |url-status=dead |title=Bazel" has refused to purchase copper combine in Serbia &#124; Forex & Finance|archive-date=2 November 2009|website=fin-forex.com}}</ref>
Basic Element built several Olympic facilities for [[2014 Winter Olympics]] in [[Sochi]], including the Coastal Olympic Village, Imeretisnkiy sea port, Doubler of Kurortny Avenue in Sochi, renovation of the [[Sochi International Airport]]. The total investments account for over $1.4 billion.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Rich Russians Sparring With Putin Over $48 Billion Olympics Bet|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2013-11-26/rich-russians-sparring-with-putin-over-48-billion-olympics-bet|work=[[Bloomberg L.P.|Bloomberg]]|access-date=14 January 2016|first1=Stephanie| last1=Baker| first2=Ilya|last2=Arkhipov|date=26 November 2013}}</ref>

During the [[2008 financial crisis]], Deripaska temporarily had to sell his 25% stake in Austrian construction company [[Strabag]], but bought them back in 2010.{{citation needed|date=February 2024}} In return, Strabag obtained a 26% stake in Transstroy.{{citation needed|date=February 2024}}

=== Troubles with US travel, 2006–2009 ===
In 2008, whilst Deripaska was involved in a bid to buy the [[Daimler Chrysler]] Group, ''[[The Guardian]]'' reported that the United States canceled his entry visa due to "criminal associations and relationships".<ref>{{cite news |title=US refused oligarch visa over alleged criminal associations |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2008/oct/31/oleg-deripaska-us-visa-rusal |website=The Guardian |date=31 October 2008 |access-date=20 May 2024 |last1=Glenny |first1=Misha |last2=Booth |first2=Robert |last3=Parfitt |first3=Tom }}</ref> ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' likewise reported that it could have been because Deripaska has been accused of having links to organized crime in Russia and cited as their sources two unnamed U.S. law enforcement officials.<ref name="reuters.com">{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSN1143738620070511|title=U.S. revoked Deripaska visa – State Dep't official|first=Jim|last=Wolf|date=11 May 2007|work=Reuters}}</ref> ''The New York Times'' reported on 27 August 2018 that the visa had been revoked on concerns Deripaska might attempt to launder money through real estate transactions.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/27/us/politics/bruce-ohr-trump-justice-department.html|title=Bruce Ohr Fought Russian Organized Crime. Now He's a Target of Trump.|newspaper=The New York Times|date=27 August 2018|access-date=29 August 2018|last1=Goldman|first1=Adam|last2=Benner|first2=Katie}}</ref> Deripaska had received a multiple-entry visa in 2005; a U.S. [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] spokesman refused to comment. Lobbying on his behalf had been done by former Senate Republican leader and 1996 presidential candidate [[Bob Dole]] and his law firm, [[Alston & Bird]], Senate records show. Alston & Bird was paid about US$260,000 in 2005 for work on "Department of State visa policies and procedures" tied to Deripaska.<ref name="reuters.com"/>

In 2009, Deripaska was again allowed entry and visited the United States twice. ''The Wall Street Journal'' reported that according to two unnamed FBI administration officials, Deripaska met with agents regarding a continuing criminal probe, the details of which were not known or reported. During Deripaska's visits, he met with leading management figures from investment banks [[Goldman Sachs]] and [[Morgan Stanley]]. The aluminium company that Deripaska headed, [[United Company RUSAL]], was in preparations for an [[initial public offering]]. The easing of Deripaska's visa issues, which were an issue for possible investors, helped to reassure bankers. The State Department has never said why it revoked his visa and refused to comment on his 2009 visits. The visits were arranged outside of the usual process as the U.S. continues to have concerns about Deripaska's business associations. Deripaska has repeatedly denied a connection to any organized crime<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stewart |first1=Sinclair |title=Oleg Deripaska |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/oleg-deripaska/article1076156/ |website=The Globe and Mail |date=11 May 2007 |access-date=20 May 2024}}</ref> and said business rivals have caused the visa to be revoked by smearing him. When interviewed by the BBC in July 2009, Deripaska said that the authorities in the United States had been attempting to blackmail him by revoking his visa and thus affecting possible investors in a negative way and thereby hoping to push Deripaska into cooperating with them.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB125687000832717809|work=The Wall Street Journal|title=Deripaska Accused U.S. of Blackmail|date=30 October 2009}}</ref>

[[NBC News]] reported in October 2021 that Russia had given Deripaska diplomatic status, allowing him to enter the U.S. with immunity.<ref name=nbcdiplo>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/fbi-agents-swarm-d-c-home-russian-oligarch-oleg-deripaska-n1281844|author1=Tom Winter|author2=Michael Kosnar|author3=Laura Strickler|title=FBI agents swarm Washington home of Russian oligarch Oleg Deripaska|website=NBC News|date=19 October 2021}}</ref>

=== Magna and lawsuit against Morgan Stanley, 2015 ===
In May 2007, [[Magna International]] chairman [[Frank Stronach]] announced that Deripaska was becoming a strategic partner in Magna.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.reportonbusiness.com/servlet/story/RTGAM.20070510.wmagna10/BNStory/robNews/home|title=Russian billionaire buying Magna stake|date=10 May 2007|work=The Globe and Mail |last=Keenan|first=Greg}}</ref> In 2007, Deripaska's Veleron [[investment vehicle]] acquired stock in Magna through a $1.2 billion loan from [[BNP Paribas]], with Magna shares serving as [[collateral (finance)|collateral]].{{citation needed|date=December 2020}} Morgan Stanley was involved in the deal through a [[Swap (finance)|swap]] agreement with BNP Paribas where the US bank assumed the risks of the loan in return for a fixed payment from Paribas.<ref name=":12">{{Cite news|title=Morgan Stanley Defeats Russian Tycoon's Short-Selling Claims|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-11-13/morgan-stanley-defeats-russian-tycoon-s-short-selling-claims-igy8py53|website=Bloomberg.com|access-date=13 January 2016|first1=Bob|last1=Van Voris|first2=Erik|last2=Larson|date=13 November 2015}}</ref>

In September 2008, Magna's stocks plummeted, hit by the global economic downturn. BNP issued a $93 million [[margin call]] to Veleron. Morgan Stanley, in turn, learned that Veleron was unlikely to meet the call and sold the stock short.<ref name=":13">{{Cite news|title=UPDATE 1-Morgan Stanley cleared in Russian tycoon's insider trading lawsuit|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/morgan-stanley-trial-idUSL1N1382UF20151113|newspaper=Reuters|date=13 November 2015|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> Deripaska claimed that Morgan Stanley abused its duties and engaged in unlawful [[insider trading]] that resulted in significant financial damage to Veleron, estimated at $15 million to $25 million.<ref name=":12"/>

In 2015, Deripaska filed a lawsuit against [[Morgan Stanley]], accusing the bank of using [[insider information]] to [[short (finance)|short sell]] Deripaska's $1.5 billion investment in shares of Canadian-based [[Magna International]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Morgan Stanley to face Russian tycoon's insider trading claims |url=http://in.reuters.com/article/morgan-stanley-trial-idINL1N12S3RO20151101|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160211210207/http://in.reuters.com/article/morgan-stanley-trial-idINL1N12S3RO20151101|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 February 2016|website=Reuters India|date=November 2015|access-date=13 January 2016|last1=Pierson|first1=Brendan}}</ref> The New York jury determined in November 2015 that Morgan Stanley had "acquired inside information and traded on it despite a duty to keep it confidential and not trade on it", finding as well that Morgan Stanley did not have the intent to [[defraud]] Veleron. Veleron strongly disagreed with and said it would file an appeal.<ref name=":13"/>{{when|date=June 2016}}

===En+ Group===
{{main|En+ Group}}
The group was formed in 2006, with Deripaska as president and controlling shareholder.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://eng.enplus.ru/about/management/|title=En+ - ведущая российская индустриальная группа, лидер в металлургии, энергетике и горнорудной промышленности|website=eng.enplus.ru|access-date=2 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728080934/http://eng.enplus.ru/about/management/|archive-date=28 July 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> The En+ Group is a diversified mining, metals and energy group. It owns a majority stake in UC Rusal&nbsp;(48.13%<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rusal.ru/en/about/facts/|title=Facts and Figures|website=rusal.ru|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref>) and in EuroSibEnergo.{{citation needed|date=March 2022}}

In 2017, it reported adjusted core earnings of $2.3 billion on revenues totaling $9.8 billion.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/russia-en-idUSL5N1H72UO|title=Russian tycoon Deripaska's En+ says 2016 core earnings $2.3 bln|date=18 April 2017|work=[[Reuters]]|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref> In November 2017, En+ was listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] raising $1.5 billion.<ref name=":9" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Davies |first=Rob |date=2022-03-10 |title=Oleg Deripaska: Putin 'favourite' with strong ties to Britain |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/mar/10/oleg-deripaska-profile-putin-britain |access-date=2022-07-06 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref>

=== Metals and mining ===

====RUSAL====
{{main|Rusal}}
[[Rusal|United Company RUSAL]] is the world's second largest aluminium company. It was the largest until it was overtaken by [[China Hongqiao Group]] in 2015. In 2019, Rusal was overtaken by China's [[Aluminum Corporation of China Limited|Chalco]] as the second biggest listed producer of aluminium.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-aluminium-chalco-idUSKCN1RA0CB|title=China's Chalco leapfrogs Rusal as second-biggest listed aluminum...|date=29 March 2019|work=Reuters|access-date=27 July 2019|language=en}}</ref> As of 2018, UC RUSAL accounts for 5.8% of the world's primary aluminium output and 6.2% of the world's alumina production.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rusal.ru/en/about/facts/|title=Rusal facts}}</ref>

In order to ensure a stable supply of alumina to its [[smelting|smelters]], several mergers and acquisitions were accomplished by RUSAL under Deripaska. At the beginning of the 2000s, RUSAL acquired bauxite mines in [[Guinea]], a country with the world's largest bauxite reserves. Subsequently, RUSAL acquired a stake in an alumina refinery in [[Australia]]. At Deripaska's behest, in 2007, RUSAL, [[SUAL Group]], one of the world's top 10 aluminium producers; and [[Glencore|Glencore International AG]], the Swiss natural resources group, merged their assets to form United Company RUSAL, the world's largest aluminium and alumina producer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-deripaska-profile-idUSTRE51L1IH20090222|title=FACTBOX: Who is Oleg Deripaska?|date=22 February 2009|access-date=14 January 2016|work=Reuters}}</ref>

After the merger with [[Glencore]], bauxite and alumina assets in [[Jamaica]], Italy and Ireland were added to RUSAL's portfolio. These transactions converted RUSAL from a company with few supplies of the raw material bauxite into a vertically integrated corporation.<ref>{{cite web|title=Без партнеров|date=18 October 2004 |url=http://www.vedomosti.ru/newspaper/articles/2004/10/18/bez-partnerov|publisher=vedomosti.ru|access-date=14 January 2016}}</ref>

In parallel, Deripaska invested significantly in the operational improvement of smelters inside Russia. He said, "We consolidated the industry, and located bauxites that do not exist in Russia. We established the company that became the leader of industry in less than twelve years. But to become the number one aluminium producer in the world, we had to improve our operations practice. To apply the best practices in the world, we looked at Toyota, which had utilized a precise, deep and well thought-through process for almost thirty years of operations."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rusal.ru/upload/uf/573/PROSPECTUS.pdf|title=United Company RUSAL Limited|publisher=RUSAL|access-date=3 June 2017|archive-date=20 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320162043/http://www.rusal.ru/upload/uf/573/PROSPECTUS.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Deripaska himself has been an active supporter of Japanese production efficiencies made popular by the "[[The Toyota Way|Toyota Way]]." RUSAL smelters have adopted the concept of ''[[kaizen]]'', which means continuous improvement and involves training workers in standardized production techniques. "It's important to change both the company's mind set and reporting lines", Deripaska said. "Instead of top-down management, you should understand everything is in the hands of your operator and empower that operator to drive efficiencies and improvements directly on the factory floor."<ref name=":0" />

Under Deripaska's leadership, RUSAL constructed and commissioned Khakas aluminium smelter outside of Sayanogorsk in Russian Siberia. The Khakas facility was the first aluminium smelter built in post-Soviet Russia (since 1985). The smelter, with an annual capacity of 300,000 tonnes, was as of 2006 one of the most technologically advanced in the world.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2006/oct/22/theobserver.observerbusiness9|title=Simon Caulkin: The world's most modern plant - and it's in Siberia|last=Caulkin|first=Simon|date=22 October 2006|website=the Guardian|language=en|access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref> The company also undertook large-scale modernization projects at a number of its facilities, including the Bratsk, Krasnoyarsk and Irkutsk aluminium smelters.<ref>{{cite web|title=HKUST IAS - UC RUSAL President's Forum|url=http://ias.ust.hk/ucrusal/2010/transcript.html|publisher=ias.ust.hk|access-date=14 January 2016}}</ref>

Deripaska returned in 2009 to RUSAL as CEO to lead the company through the debt restructuring process. "I worked 16-hour days. We were in default, although none of the parties involved wanted to call it default." As part of contingency measures, Deripaska cut costs at RUSAL by 25% in 2009. By December 2009, Deripaska reached a final agreement with over 70 Russian and international lenders to refinance US$17 billion of debt.<ref name=":0" />

In 2017, Rusal issued two [[Eurobond (international)|Eurobonds]] to finance its debts. The first one, worth $600 million, was issued in February,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://aluminiuminsider.com/rusal-prices-initial-eurobond |title=Rusal Prices Initial Eurobond |date=30 January 2017|work=Aluminium Insider| access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref> followed by the second one in April, worth $500 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/1084218c-2cdc-355b-a52f-7887fb4aea59|title=Rusal profit amid rebound in aluminium prices|work=Financial Times|date=12 May 2017|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref> Also in February, plans were announced to sell 10 billion yuan worth of seven-year onshore bonds to finance purchases in China. This made Rusal the first foreign company to offer [[panda bonds]] on the [[Shanghai Stock Exchange]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.scmp.com/business/companies/article/2069488/aluminium-giant-rusal-plans-10-billion-yuan-panda-bond-issue|title=Rusal plans 10 billion yuan panda bond issue in Shanghai|work=South China Morning Post|date=9 February 2017|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref> The company also agreed on a pre-export finance mechanism with international lenders worth $1.7 billion for debt refinancing.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://aluminiuminsider.com/rusal-negotiates-us1-7-bn-pxf-debt-facility |title=Rusal Negotiates US$1.7 BN PXF Debt Facility |date=26 May 2017|work=Aluminium Insider|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref>

In 2013, Deripaska was awarded the "Aluminium Industry Ambassador Award" in the ''[[Metal Bulletin]]'' Awards for Excellence for his "great influence within the global aluminium industry and the wider market".<ref>{{cite web|title=Winners of Metal Bulletin's awards for aluminium excellence 2013|url=http://www.metalbulletin.com/Article/3256866/Search/Winners-of-Metal-Bulletins-awards-for-aluminium-excellence.html|work=[[Metal Bulletin]]|access-date=14 January 2016}}</ref>

Deripaska stepped down from RUSAL in May 2018 the day after seven board members and the chief executive resigned. The move was part of a deal with the US Treasury to get U.S. sanctions removed from the company.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sanctioned Tycoon Deripaska Resigns as Director of His Firm Rusal|url=https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2018/05/25/business/25reuters-usa-russia-sanctions-rusal.html|website=[[The New York Times]]|date=25 May 2018|access-date=27 May 2018|agency=Reuters|last1=Devitt|first1=Polina|last2=Voronova|first2=Tatiana|last3=Korsunskaya|first3=Darya|last4=Lowe|first4=Christian|editor-last=Anantharaman|editor-first=Muralikumar}}</ref> As part of that deal, in February 2019 it was announced that Deripaska had reduced his ownership stake in EN+ to below 50% in order to obtain sanctions relief.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.economist.com/business/2019/02/02/america-lifts-sanctions-on-oleg-deripaskas-business-empire|title=America lifts sanctions on Oleg Deripaska's business empire|date=2 February 2019|newspaper=The Economist|access-date=6 February 2019|issn=0013-0613}}</ref>

=====Cherney lawsuit, 2008 =====
[[Michael Cherney]] brought legal action against Deripaska in the [[Commercial Court (England and Wales)|Commercial Court]] of the [[High Court]] in London.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/the-worlds-richest-russian-is-sued-for-3bn-in-london-437814.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080610171148/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/the-worlds-richest-russian-is-sued-for-3bn-in-london-437814.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 June 2008|title=The world's richest Russian is sued for $3bn in London|work=The Independent|location=UK|date=25 February 2007|access-date=14 May 2011|first=Andrew|last=Osborn}}</ref> Cherney sought a declaration that he was the beneficial owner of 20% of [[RUSAL]] stock which, he claimed, Deripaska held in trust for him. The claim was denied. On 3 May 2007, Justice Langley ruled that Deripaska had not been properly [[service of process|served]], and that the court had no [[jurisdiction]] to try the claim as Deripaska did not live in England or Wales.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWHC/Comm/2007/965.html|title=''Cherney v Deripaska'', 2007 EWHC 965 (Comm)|publisher=Bailii.org|access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref>

In July 2008, Justice Christopher Clarke ruled that the case should be tried in England, although "the natural forum for this litigation is Russia", because, he held, "risks inherent in a trial in Russia...are sufficient to make England the forum in which the case can most suitably be tried in the interest of both parties and the ends of justice".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWHC/Comm/2008/1530.html|title=''Cherney v Deripaska'', 2008 EWHC 1530 (Comm)|publisher=Bailii.org|access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref> On 22 July 2008, he granted Deripaska the right to appeal. The Court of Appeal of England and Wales rejected the appeal on 31 July 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2009/849.html|title=Deripaska v Cherney, 2009 EWCA Civ 849|publisher=Bailii.org|access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref>

At a June 2011 case management conference, the judge deferred a decision on whether Cherney would be allowed to give evidence by video link from Israel rather than appear in person. An outstanding arrest warrant issued by [[Interpol]] meant that the British would detain him if he travelled to the UK.<ref>Paul, Jonny. (23 June 2011) [https://www.jpost.com/International/Article.aspx?id=226187&R=R4 "British High Court to decide: Can Cherney testify by video?"] ''The Jerusalem Post''. 23 June 2011. Retrieved 12 May 2012.</ref><ref name="Interpol">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090928225838/http://www.interpol.int/public/Data/Wanted/Notices/Data/2009/42/2009_21842.asp "Wanted: Cherney, Michael"]. [[Interpol]], (14 October 2010)</ref> In late July 2011, the High Court ruled to allow Cherney to give evidence at the trial by video link from Israel, and also set trial for April 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/standard/article-23973334-the-gangster-a-billionaire-friend-of-mandelson-and-a-pound-23bn-row.do |title=The 'gangster', a billionaire friend of Mandelson and a £2.3bn row|work=Evening Standard|first=Paul|last=Cheston|date=28 July 2011|access-date=8 August 2011| url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222031121/http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/standard/article-23973334-the-gangster-a-billionaire-friend-of-mandelson-and-a-pound-23bn-row.do|archive-date=22 February 2012}}</ref> Deripaska denied that Cherney was owed any stake in RUSAL, and asserted payments made to Cherney had been for unavoidable "protection" at a time when violence was sweeping the region and posed an existential threat to any profitable business in the country. In an interview with ''The Telegraph'', Deripaska said he was one of the few who worked to clean up Russian industry and provided support to law enforcement agencies. However, in this early chaotic period paying protection money to criminal gangs was inescapable, as revealed in court testimony.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Oleg Deripaska: Why I paid crime gangs for protection| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/industry/mining/9218657/Oleg-Deripaska-Why-I-paid-crime-gangs-for-protection.html|work=The Telegraph | date=21 April 2012|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> In September 2012, Cherney terminated his UK lawsuit against Deripaska.<ref name="Suit Against Russian Billionaire Is Dropped, WSJ">{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10000872396390444549204578022433469797910 |title=Suit Against Russian Billionaire Is Dropped|work=The Wall Street Journal|first1=Paul|last1=Sonne|first2=Alexander|last2=Kolyandr|date=27 September 2012|access-date=7 November 2012}}</ref>

===Energy===

==== EuroSibEnergo ====
EuroSibEnergo controls and manages 18 power plants with a combined installed energy capacity of 19.5 GW, including 15 GW provided by hydrogeneration. The company produces approximately 9% of all electricity in [[Russia]] and is also the leader in the Siberian energy market, with a market share totaling 41%. Some of EuroSibEnergo's key clients include the largest aluminium plants in Russia. The company owns large fuel resources, which satisfy over 85% of the coal needs of its thermal power and boiler plants. Its coal reserves amount to 1.26 billion tons, with annual coal production exceeding 12 million tons.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web|title=EuroSibEnergo (Russia): Global Sustainable Electricity Partnership|url=http://www.globalelectricity.org/en/index.jsp?p=324|website=globalelectricity.org|access-date=13 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160207221639/http://www.globalelectricity.org/en/index.jsp?p=324|archive-date=7 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>
 
En+ Group, of which EuroSibEnergo is a subsidiary, is investing in a joint venture with China's largest [[hydroelectric power]] generation company [[China Yangtze Power]] Co to build new power plants in Siberia, primarily hydroelectric ones, with a total capacity of up to 10 GWt.<ref>{{Cite web|title=China Three Gorges, En+ eye projects in Russia|url=http://www.chinadailyasia.com/business/2015-10/30/content_15337032.html|work=[[China Daily Asia]]|date=30 October 2015|access-date=13 January 2016}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

===Machinery===

====Russian Machines====
Russian Machines corporation was established in 2005 and unites Deripaska's machine building assets. It comprises industrial and engineering assets in the following industries: automotive OEM (GAZ Group), automotive components (RM-Systems), rail industry (RM Rail), aircraft OEM (Aviacor), road construction (RM-Terex) and agricultural machinery (AGCO-RM).<ref name="bloomberg.com">{{Cite web|title=GAZ Group: Private Company Information |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapid=8954451|work=[[Businessweek]]|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref>

Russian Machines Corporation manages 24 facilities located across 12 regions in Russia.<ref name="bloomberg.com"/>

In September 2017, Deripaska entered into a joint venture through his Russian Machines ({{langx|ru|«Русские машины»}}) with [[AGCO]] called AGCO-RM SPIC project ({{langx|ru|проекта СПИКа АГКО-РМ}}).<ref>{{cite news |last=Циноева |first=Яна (Tsinoeva, Yana) |url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/3407851 |title=Американские трактора буксуют на СПИКе: "Русские машины" и Минпромторг спорят об условиях контракта |trans-title=American tractors skid on SPIK: Russian Machines and the Ministry of Industry and Trade are arguing about the terms of the contract |language=ru |work=[[Kommersant]] |date=11 September 2017 |access-date=29 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Джумайло |first1=Анатолий (Dzhumaylo, Anatoly) |last2=Дзагуто |first2=Владимир (Dzaguto, Vladimir) |last3=Циноева |first3=Яна (Tsinoeva, Yana) |last4=Райский |first4=Андрей (Raysky, Andrey) |last5=Ладыгин |first5=Дмитрий (Ladygin, Dmitry) |last6=Тарасенко |first6=Павел (Tarasenko, Pavel) |last7=Строкань |first7=Сергей (Strokan, Sergey) |last8=Черненко |first8=Елена (Chernenko, Elena) |url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/3597822 |title=38 попугали: Санкции США довели до российских миллиардеров |trans-title=38 parrots: US sanctions brought to Russian billionaires |language=ru |work=[[Kommersant]] |date=6 April 2018 |access-date=29 March 2022}} [http://www.compromat.ru/page_39005.htm Alternate archive] as За "разнообразную злонамеренную деятельность": "Близкие к Кремлю" миллиардеры Дерипаска, Вексельберг и Керимов под санкциями США (For "various malicious activities": "Close to the Kremlin" billionaires Deripaska, Vekselberg and Kerimov under US sanctions)</ref>

====GAZ Group====
In 2000, Deripaska started acquiring machine building assets. His first acquisition was [[Nizhny Novgorod]]-based Gorkovsky Automobile Plant (GAZ), which was previously a government-run company. In 2005, [[GAZ Group]] was established by combining Deripaska's machine building assets.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Russian GAZ Starts Chrysler Sebring Based Siber Production|url=http://www.carscoops.com/2008/07/russian-gaz-starts-chrysler-sebring.html|work=CarScoops|access-date=13 January 2016|date=28 July 2008}}</ref>

The Russian automotive conglomerate, GAZ Group, comprises 18 manufacturing facilities in eight regions of Russia, as well as sales and service organizations. GAZ Group produces light and medium commercial vehicles, heavy trucks, buses, cars, road construction equipment, power units, and automotive components.<ref name="bloomberg.com" />
 
In March 2019, GAZ Group asked the [[Government of Russia|Russian government]] for $468 million in support claiming that US sanctions placed on Deripaska could cut production by almost 40% in the second half of that year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2019/04/18/sanctions-hit-gaz-wants-government-bail-out-kommersant-a65290|title=Sanctions-hit GAZ Wants Government Bail-Out – Kommersant|date=18 April 2019|website=The Moscow Times|language=en|access-date=27 July 2019}}</ref>

====Airports====
Basel Aero, a joint venture between Changi Airports International, Basic Element and Sberbank of Russia, is a company-operator the [[Sochi International Airport|Sochi]], [[Krasnodar International Airport|Krasnodar]] and [[Anapa Airport|Anapa airports]].<ref name="airport-world.com">{{Cite web|title=Sochi airport prepares for Winter Olympics - Airport World Magazine|url=http://www.airport-world.com/news/general-news/2923-sochi-airport-prepares-for-winter-olympics.html|website=airport-world.com|access-date=13 January 2016|archive-date=8 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160208170108/http://www.airport-world.com/news/general-news/2923-sochi-airport-prepares-for-winter-olympics.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

These airports handle more than 7% of the total passenger flow in Russia.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Behind the scenes as Sochi Airport warms up for the 2014 Winter Olympic Games|url=http://www.airport-technology.com/features/featuresochi-airport-winter-olympic-games-technology-4160035/|website=Airport Technology |date=15 January 2014|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> Sochi International Airport was the main gateway to Sochi [[2014 Winter Olympics]] and successfully serviced the guests and participants of the Games.<ref name="airport-world.com"/>

In October 2014, Sochi was granted [[open skies]] status, meaning that any foreign carrier may pick up and drop off passengers and cargo with no restrictions on aircraft type, frequency, and regardless of interstate agreements.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sochi International Airport: Russia under wide Open Skies|url=http://www.basel.ru/en/in_focus/baselaero_23_03_2015/|work=basel.ru|access-date=13 January 2016|date=23 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160208170115/http://www.basel.ru/en/in_focus/baselaero_23_03_2015/|archive-date=8 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Financial services===
Deripaska personally holds 10% of [[Ingosstrakh]]'s ordinary shares. The company is a leading insurer of complex risks such as [[Marine insurance|insurance]] for ship owners, ship hull insurance, insurance against aviation and space-related risks, and insurance of transportation companies. Ingosstrakh has 83 branches in Russia and the company's offices operate in 220 Russian towns and cities.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Deripaska Insurer's Volkov Says Ingosstrakh to Lease Out Planes|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2010-11-22/deripaska-insurer-s-volkov-says-ingosstrakh-to-lease-out-planes|work=Bloomberg|access-date=13 January 2016|first=Ilya|last=Khrennikov|date=22 November 2010}}</ref>

===Agribusiness===
In 2011, Deripaska established Kuban Agroholding, a 75,000-hectare [[agribusiness]] in the Krasnodar region.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2 June 2011|title=Deripaska Farm Ready for Grain Exports|url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2011/06/02/deripaska-farm-ready-for-grain-exports-a7378|access-date=12 March 2021|website=The Moscow Times|language=en}}</ref> The company integrates two dairy farms, а 16,000 pig capacity breeding complex, three [[Grain elevator|elevators]] with non-recurrent grain storage capacity of more than 270,000 tonnes, three grain processing plants, a sugar factory and the Sunrise horse breeding farm, specializing in the breeding of English [[thoroughbred]] horses. It is one of the top-20 largest agribusinesses and top-5 most efficient land users in Russia.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Russia's Kuban Agroholding launches slaughterhouses, hog farm| url=https://issuu.com/farmingmonthly/docs/february_2015_farming_monthly_natio/12?e=15147366/11395275|journal=Farming Monthly|date=February 2015|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref>

Kuban Agroholding is one of the few agrocompanies in Russia involved in [[embryo transfer]] technology that allows for the reproduction of high-yielding milk cows using less-productive surrogates.<ref name="agra-net.com">{{Cite web|title=Interview: R&D and innovation are key in race to boost Russia's farm output|url=https://www.agra-net.com/agra/agra-europe/analysis/interview-rd-and-innovation-are-key-in-race-to-boost-russia-s-farm-output-467790.htm|work=Agra-net.com|access-date=13 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160203194802/https://www.agra-net.com/agra/agra-europe/analysis/interview-rd-and-innovation-are-key-in-race-to-boost-russia-s-farm-output-467790.htm|archive-date=3 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The company has gained significant media attention for its corn-seeding program, deploying several dozen corn brands selected by its genetic specialists.<ref name="agra-net.com"/>

According to [[Forbes]] in June 2019, Deripaska's Kuban land bank was the fourteenth largest in Russia.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Попов |first1=Игорь (Popov, Igor) |last2=Ляликова |first2=Анастасия (Lyalikova, Anastasia) |last3=Плешков |first3=Максим (Pleshkov, Maxim) |url=https://www.forbes.ru/milliardery-photogallery/378069-hozyaeva-zemli-russkoy-20-samyh-dorogih-zemlevladeniy-rossii-reyting |title=Хозяева земли русской: 20 самых дорогих землевладений России. Рейтинг Forbes |trans-title=The owners of the Russian land: 20 most expensive land holdings in Russia. Forbes rating |language=ru |work=[[Forbes]] |date=17 June 2019 |access-date=29 March 2022 |archive-date=30 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220330022603/https://www.forbes.ru/milliardery-photogallery/378069-hozyaeva-zemli-russkoy-20-samyh-dorogih-zemlevladeniy-rossii-reyting}} [http://www.compromat.ru/page_40333.htm Alternate archive]</ref>

===Redut PMC===
{{Main|Redut (company)}}
Redut, also known as Redoubt or Redut-Antiterror and formerly known as "Shield",<ref name="infantry">{{Cite web |date=10 August 2022 |title=Пехота пуще неволи |trans-title=Infantry is worse than a jail time|url=https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2022/08/10/pekhota-pushche-nevoli |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220814111043/https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2022/08/10/pekhota-pushche-nevoli |archive-date=14 August 2022 |access-date=19 June 2023 |website=[[Novaya Gazeta]] |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 November 2022 |title=Зона поражения |trans-title=The kill zone|url=https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2022/11/10/zona-porazheniia |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230620114054/https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2022/11/10/zona-porazheniia |archive-date=20 June 2023 |access-date=20 June 2023 |website=[[Novaya Gazeta]] |language=ru}}</ref> is a Russian [[Private military company|Private Military and Security Company]] (PMSC) that is part of the "Antiterror-family". Redut consists of similarly named PMSCs which protect commercial operations of Russian companies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=РЕГИОНАЛЬНАЯ ОБЩЕСТВЕННАЯ ОРГАНИЗАЦИЯ "ВЕТЕРАНОВ МИРОТВОРЧЕСКИХ МИССИЙ И ЛОКАЛЬНЫХ КОНФЛИКТОВ" |trans-title=REGIONAL PUBLIC ORGANIZATION "VETERANS OF PEACEKEEPING MISSIONS AND LOCAL CONFLICTS"|url=https://zachestnyibiznes.ru/company/ul/1077799027547_7713386568_ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190708000118/https://zachestnyibiznes.ru/company/ul/1077799027547_7713386568_#selection-1591.0-1591.81 |archive-date=8 July 2019 |access-date=3 May 2023 |website=Registry for the Association of Veterans of Peacekeeping and Local Conflict Missions (Zachestnyibiznes)}}</ref> Redut is currently deployed by [[Russia]] in the [[Russian invasion of |archive-date=9 May 2022 |access-date=3 May 2023 |website=New America}}</ref><ref name="sanctions">{{Cite web |title=Private Military Company Redut |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427235812/https://www.opensanctions.org/entities/NK-9iEp7sqxGYKEzvhd2qyeWC/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="human">{{Cite web |title=Long sentences passed on 'Redut' mercenaries fighting Russia's war against Ukraine with Finnish citizen's funding |url=https://khpg.org/en/1608811793 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230503191107/https://khpg.org/en/1608811793 |archive-date=3 May 2023 |access-date=3 May 2023 |website=[[Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite Research Establishment (FFI)}}</ref> for which it was sanctioned.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 April 2021 |title=Blocking Property With Respect To Specified Harmful Foreign Activities of the Government of the Russian Federation |url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2021/04/19/2021-08098/blocking-property-with-respect-to-specified-harmful-foreign-activities-of-the-government-of-the |archive-date=27 April 2021 |access-date=11 June 2023 |website=[[Federal Register]]}}</ref> Several fighters of the group have been convicted of war crimes during the invasion.<ref name="human"/>

Oleg Deripaska and [[Gennady Timchenko]] reportedly are major backers of the company. The PMC received [[Armoured personnel carrier|armored personnel carriers]], helmets, and protective vests from them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=svizzera |first=RSINews, l’informazione della Radiotelevisione |title=Mercenari russi e quel legame con la Svizzera |trans-title=Russian mercenaries and their connection to Switzerland|url=https://www.rsi.ch/news/mondo/Mercenari-russi-e-quel-legame-con-la-Svizzera-15978238.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230305114914/https://www.rsi.ch/news/mondo/Mercenari-russi-e-quel-legame-con-la-Svizzera-15978238.html |archive-date=5 March 2023 |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=rsi |date=30 January 2023 |language=it}}</ref><ref name="bluewin.ch">{{Cite web |title=Die Spur einer Söldnerbande führt auch in die Schweiz |trans-title=The trail of a mercenary band also leads to Switzerland|url=https://www.bluewin.ch/de/news/schweiz/das-verbindet-russische-soeldner-mit-der-schweiz-1606961.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230503191805/https://www.bluewin.ch/de/news/schweiz/das-verbindet-russische-soeldner-mit-der-schweiz-1606961.html |archive-date=3 May 2023 |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=blue News |language=de}}</ref>
