=== Other roles ===
In 2004, Deripaska was appointed by the [[President of Russia]] to represent the country in the [[Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation]] [[Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation#APEC Business Advisory Council|Business Advisory Council]] (ABAC). He has been Chairman of ABAC Russia since 2007. Deripaska is the vice president of the [[Russian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs]], chairman of the executive board of the Russian national committee of the [[International Chamber of Commerce]] and a member of the Competitiveness and Entrepreneurship Council, an agency of the Russian government.<ref>[http://www.deripaska.com/about-oleg-deripaska/biography Oleg Deripaska biodata] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721132612/http://www.deripaska.com/about-oleg-deripaska/biography|date=21 July 2011}}. Retrieved 12 May 2012.</ref>

Since 2007, he has been a permanent participant at [[World Economic Forum]] sessions, when RUSAL became a WEF "strategic partner".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Oleg V. Deripaska|url=http://www.weforum.org/contributors/oleg-v-deripaska|publisher=[[World Economic Forum]]|access-date=13 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150404232416/http://www.weforum.org/contributors/oleg-v-deripaska|archive-date=4 April 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Investigations==
In 2009, Deripaska had been interrogated as a witness in Spain and England and by the FBI about [[money laundering]], he was never charged with any crimes.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB125685578903317087 |work=The Wall Street Journal |title=FBI Lets Barred Tycoon Visit U.S |first1=Evan |last1=Perez |first2=Gregory L. |last2=White |date=30 October 2009}}</ref> 
On 25 January 2010, the ''[[Financial Times]]'' published a story titled "Rusal: A lingering heat" exploring Deripaska's business relations with Sergei Popov and Anton Malevsky, alleged heads of Russian organized crime groups.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/70a1c458-09ff-11df-8b23-00144feabdc0 |title=/ Comment / Analysis – Rusal: A lingering heat |work=Financial Times |date=25 January 2010 |access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref> Deripaska has accused Michael Chernoy of using Malevsky and the [[Izmaylovskaya gang|Izmailovskaya syndicate]] to extort US$250&nbsp;million from him as part of a protection racket.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/clash-of-the-oligarchs-1753022.html|title=Clash of the oligarchs|work=The Independent|location=UK|date=20 July 2009|access-date=14 May 2011|first=Donald|last=MacIntyre}}</ref> However, Deripaska has himself been accused of having similar links to Malevsky, who, with his brother Andrei, owned a 10% stake in Deripaska's company. Deripaska denies the claims.<ref>Swinford, Steven, "Peter Mandelson oligarch Oleg Deripaska linked to mafia boss", ''The Sunday Times'' (London), 26 October 2008.</ref>
In 2011, Deripaska and [[Iskander Makhmudov]] (head of UGMK) were asked by Spanish police to answer questions in relation to a money-laundering enquiry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elmundo.es/papel/2010/03/21/mercados/23228430.html |title=Quiosco, El Mundo en ORBYT |work=El Mundo|location=Spain |access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref>

In November 2011, Spain's High Court sent the criminal cases against Deripaska to the Russian General Prosecutor's office because the root of the cases is Russian.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://en.gazeta.ru/news/2011/11/25/a_3848274.shtml|title=Russian Tycoon Deripaska's case given to Russia's court by Spain|publisher=gazeta.ru|first=Darya|last=Ispolnova|date=25 November 2011|access-date=28 November 2011|archive-date=15 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120415095926/http://en.gazeta.ru/news/2011/11/25/a_3848274.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Political relationships and controversies==
[[File:Vladimir Putin 19 March 2002-4.jpg|thumb|[[Vladimir Putin]] and Deripaska, 19 March 2002]]

===Vladimir Putin===
Deripaska is known for his close ties with Russian president [[Vladimir Putin]]. Their relationship became visibly strained amidst Deripaska's financial struggles in 2009. In an incident broadcast on Russian television, Putin visited a stalled cement factory owned by Deripaska and berated its management. He forced Deripaska to sign a contract promising to pay nearly $1 million in unpaid wages.<ref name="globeandmail2011"/><ref>{{cite news|last1=Oliphant|first1=Roland|title=Fifteen years of Vladimir Putin: in quotes|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/vladimir-putin/11588182/Fifteen-years-of-Vladimir-Putin-in-quotes.html|access-date=25 May 2017|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=7 May 2015|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Reynolds|first1=Leda|title=ISIS beware: THIS is how hardman Russian President Vladimir Putin gets things DONE|url=https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/610552/ISIS-beware-THIS-is-how-hardman-Vladimir-Putin-gets-things-DONE|access-date=25 May 2017|work=The Express| date=7 October 2015|language=en}}</ref> Their relationship recovered, however, and Deripaska has been described as "Putin's favorite [[Business magnate|industrialist]]".<ref>{{cite news|last1=Marcin|first1=Tim|title=Meet Oleg Deripaska, who allegedly worked with former Trump aide Paul Manafort to push Putin's views| url=https://www.newsweek.com/who-oleg-deripaska-paul-manafort-russian-putin-572157|access-date=25 May 2017|work=Newsweek|date=22 March 2017|language=en}}</ref> [[United States diplomatic cables leak|Leaked U.S. diplomatic cables]] from 2006 described Deripaska as "among the 2–3 oligarchs Putin turns to on a regular basis" and "a more-or-less permanent fixture on Putin's trips abroad".<ref name="ap32217">{{cite news|last1=Horowitz| first1=Jeff|last2=Day|first2=Chad|title=AP findings on Trump associate's work for Russian oligarch|url=https://apnews.com/ba0027b4c29a4863b096d7216ee0ca58/ap-findings-trump-associates-work-russian-oligarch|access-date=25 May 2017|work=[[Associated Press]]|date=22 March 2017}}</ref> In a 2011 interview with ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', [[Kinross Gold]] CEO Tye Burt, who knows Deripaska, said "I believe Russia recognizes Oleg's major role in building a renewed economic base in a broad range of domestic businesses and rejuvenating ailing companies and infrastructure."<ref name="globeandmail2011"/>

===Nathaniel Rothschild and Peter Mandelson===
Deripaska is a friend of [[Nathaniel Rothschild, 5th Baron Rothschild|Nathaniel Rothschild]], a major investor in both [[Glencore]] and [[United Company RUSAL]]. Together Deripaska and Rothschild hosted [[George Osborne]] and [[Peter Mandelson]] on Deripaska's yacht in [[Corfu]] in the summer of 2008.<ref>
{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/opinion/leading-articles/leading-article-the-flawed-judgement-of-a-shadow-chancellor-968549.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100723091059/http://www.independent.co.uk/opinion/leading-articles/leading-article-the-flawed-judgement-of-a-shadow-chancellor-968549.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 July 2010|title=Leading article: The flawed judgement of a shadow Chancellor|date=22 October 2008|work=The Independent|location=UK|access-date=23 November 2009}}</ref> Osborne was then Shadow [[Chancellor of the Exchequer]] of the United Kingdom and a friend of Rothschild from school and university. [[Peter Mandelson]] has reportedly maintained private contacts over several years with Deripaska.<ref name=mandelson>{{cite news|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/politics/article4982163.ece|title=Lord Mandelson and Oleg Deripaska dined together 'a year before they met'|last=Robertson|first=David|date=21 October 2008|newspaper=[[The Times]]|location=UK|access-date=23 October 2008}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

News of the contacts sparked criticism because, as European Union Trade Commissioner, Mandelson had been responsible for decision to cut aluminium tariffs from 6 to 3%, a decision that had benefited Deripaska's Company [[RusAl]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.moscowtimes.ru/article/1010/42/371829.htm|title=UK Conservatives Linked to Deripaska|date=22 October 2008|newspaper=[[The Moscow Times]] |access-date=23 October 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081126051311/http://www.moscowtimes.ru/article/1010/42/371829.htm|archive-date=26 November 2008}}</ref> Mandelson insisted that he had never discussed aluminium tariffs with Deripaska.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/politics/article4932191.ece|title=Peter Mandelson dogged by his links to Russian oligarch|date=13 October 2008|newspaper=[[The Times]]|last2=Charter|first2=David|location=UK|access-date=23 October 2008|first1=David|last1=Robertson}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On 26 October 2008 the [[Shadow Foreign Secretary]] [[William Hague]] claimed the "whole country" wanted "transparency" about Mandelson's previous meetings with Deripaska. In response, Prime Minister [[Gordon Brown]] said Mandelson's dealings with Deripaska had been "found to be above board".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/politics/7691678.stm|title=Tories seek Mandelson 'clarity'|date=26 October 2008|work=BBC News|access-date=30 October 2008}}</ref> Mandelson said that meeting business figures from "across the range" in emerging economies was part of his brief as EU Trade Commissioner.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2008/oct/28/peter-mandelson-oleg-deripaska-corfu|title=Mandelson silent on Deripaska|last=Parfitt|first=Tom|date=28 October 2008|newspaper=The Guardian|location=UK|access-date=30 October 2008}}</ref> On 29 October 2008, while Mandelson was on a ministerial visit to Moscow,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2008/oct/29/russia-mandelson|title=Mandelson hails thaw in relations with Moscow|last=Parfitt|first=Tom|date=29 October 2008|work=The Guardian|location=UK|access-date=30 October 2008}}</ref> it was alleged in the British press that Valery Pechenkin, the head of security at Deripaska's company [[Basic Element (company)|Basic Element]], organised a swift entry visa for Mandelson when he came to Moscow to visit Deripaska in 2005.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/homesandproperty/property-news/abramovich-s-right-hand-man-bids-to-turn-crumbling-kensington-hotel-into-luxury-flats-b990522.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081101053919/http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/standard/article-23579423-details/Veteran+KGB+spy+revealed+as+Deripaska%27s+right-hand+man/article.do|url-status=live|archive-date=1 November 2008|title=Veteran KGB spy revealed as Deripaska's right-hand man|date=29 October 2008|work=[[London Evening Standard]]|access-date=30 October 2008}}</ref>

===Paul Manafort===
On 22 March 2017, the [[Associated Press]] published a report alleging that [[Paul Manafort]], [[Donald Trump]]'s former presidential campaign manager, negotiated a $10 million annual contract with Deripaska to promote Russian interests in politics, business, and media coverage in Europe and the United States, starting in 2005.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.apnews.com/122ae0b5848345faa88108a03de40c5a/Manafort%27s-plan-to-%27greatly-benefit-the-Putin-Government|title=Trump campaign chief linked to Putin interests|last=HORWITZ and DAY|date=22 March 2017|work=Associated Press|access-date=22 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170402165112/https://www.apnews.com/122ae0b5848345faa88108a03de40c5a/Manafort%27s-plan-to-%27greatly-benefit-the-Putin-Government|archive-date=2 April 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Both Deripaska and Manafort confirmed working together in the past,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/know-paul-manafort-links-oleg-224806634.html|title=What We Know About Paul Manafort's Links to Oleg Deripaska and the Kremlin|access-date=5 April 2017|language=en-US|archive-date=5 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405174032/https://www.yahoo.com/news/know-paul-manafort-links-oleg-224806634.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> but rejected the contents of the AP story. Manafort argued that his work had been inaccurately presented, and that there was nothing “inappropriate or nefarious" about it.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/international/russia/326170-russian-billionaire-i-didnt-aid-putin-with-manafort/|title=Russian billionaire denies aiding Putin with Manafort|last=Hensch|first=Mark|date=28 March 2017|work=The Hill|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jan/29/oleg-deripaska-paul-manafort-trump-russia-investigation|title=Is Oleg Deripaska the missing link in the Trump-Russia investigation?|website=[[TheGuardian.com]]|date=29 January 2019}}</ref>

Responding to the allegations, on 28 March 2017, Deripaska published open letters in the print editions of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' and ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' in which he denied having signed a $10 million contract with Manafort in order to benefit the [[Russia under Vladimir Putin|Putin government]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/russian-manafort-client-willing-to-speak-to-congress/2017/03/28/1add6c1a-13e9-11e7-bb16-269934184168_story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328220816/https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/russian-manafort-client-willing-to-speak-to-congress/2017/03/28/1add6c1a-13e9-11e7-bb16-269934184168_story.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 March 2017|title=Russian Manafort client: Willing to speak to Congress|newspaper=Washington Post| access-date=5 April 2017}}</ref> He also stated willingness to testify before the [[United States Congress]] about these allegations,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/russian-manafort-client-willing-to-speak-to-congress/2017/03/28/1add6c1a-13e9-11e7-bb16-269934184168_story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328220816/https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/russian-manafort-client-willing-to-speak-to-congress/2017/03/28/1add6c1a-13e9-11e7-bb16-269934184168_story.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 March 2017|title=Russian Manafort client: Willing to speak to Congress|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=5 April 2017}}</ref> and argued that the accusations were part of "the negative context of current US-Russian relations."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/russian-billionaire-oleg-deripaska-paul-manafort-ties-donald-trump-campaign-manager-us-congress-a7655291.html|title=Russian billionaire with ties to Trump's ex-campaign manager says he is willing to testify before Congress|date=29 March 2017|work=The Independent|access-date=4 April 2017|language=en-GB}}</ref> Congressional sources cited by ''[[The New York Times]]'' said lawmakers declined Deripaska's request{{Clarification needed|date=January 2023}} after he had asked for immunity from criminal prosecution. Unnamed officials argued that "immunity agreements create complications for federal criminal investigators".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/05/26/us/politics/oleg-deripaska-paul-manafort.html|title=Russian Once Tied to Trump Aide Seeks Immunity to Cooperate With Congress|last1=Meier|first1=Barry|date=26 May 2017|work=The New York Times|access-date=2 June 2017|last2=Drucker|first2=Jesse|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

On 15 May 2017, Deripaska filed a defamation and libel lawsuit against the [[Associated Press]] in [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia|U.S. District Court in D.C.]], arguing that<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/f/?id=0000015c-0e98-de0a-a15e-1f9900d90000|title=''Oleg V. Deripaska v. The Associated Press''|publisher=[[United States District Court for the District of Columbia]]|date=15 May 2017|access-date=27 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fortune.com/2017/05/16/donald-trump-paul-manafort-campaign-ap-lawsuit |title=Russian Magnate Sues AP Over Story on Trump Campaign Ties|website=Fortune|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> the report falsely claimed that Deripaska had signed a contract with Manafort to advance the goals of the Russian government.<ref name=":7">{{Cite news|url=https://www.politico.com/blogs/under-the-radar/2017/05/15/russian-oligarch-deripaska-manafort-238419|title=Russian oligarch Deripaska sues AP for libel|work=[[Politico]]|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> The lawsuit was dismissed in October 2017 on the grounds that Deripaska had not disputed "any material facts" in the story by the Associated Press.<ref name="Rybka">{{cite news|url=https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-rybkagate-rolls-on-sex-lies-instagram-deripaska-prikhodko/29031221.html|title=Sex, Lies, And Instagram: Russia's 'Rybkagate' Rolls On|newspaper=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty|date=9 February 2018 |access-date=5 March 2018|last1=Schreck |first1=Carl}}</ref>

While Manafort served within the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 U.S. presidential campaign]], it is alleged that Manafort, via [[Kyiv]]-based operative [[Konstantin Kilimnik]], offered to provide briefings on political developments to Deripaska.<ref name="WaPo">{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/manafort-offered-to-give-russian-billionaire-private-briefings-on-2016-campaign/2017/09/20/399bba1a-9d48-11e7-8ea1-ed975285475e_story.html |date=20 September 2017 |title=Manafort offered to give Russian billionaire 'private briefings' on 2016 campaign |first1=Tom |last1=Hamburger |first2=Rosalind S. |last2=Helderman |first3=Carol D. |last3=Leonnig |first4=Adam |last4=Entous |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921003301/https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/manafort-offered-to-give-russian-billionaire-private-briefings-on-2016-campaign/2017/09/20/399bba1a-9d48-11e7-8ea1-ed975285475e_story.html |archive-date=21 September 2017 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |publisher=[[Politico]] |title=Manafort used Trump campaign account to email Ukrainian operative |first=Josh |last=Dawsey |date=20 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921003929/http://www.politico.com/story/2017/09/20/paul-manafort-trump-campaign-email-ukrainian-operative-242949 |archive-date=21 September 2017 |url-status=live |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2017/09/20/paul-manafort-trump-campaign-email-ukrainian-operative-242949}}</ref> Behaviors such as these were seen by writers at ''[[The Atlantic]]'' as an attempt by Manafort "to please an oligarch tied to" Putin's government.<ref name=ioffeman>{{cite web|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/archive/2017/10/emails-suggest-manafort-sought-approval-from-putin-ally-deripaska/541677 |title=Did Manafort Use Trump to Curry Favor With a Putin Ally? Emails turned over to investigators detail the former campaign chair's efforts to please an oligarch tied to the Kremlin. |author=[[Julia Ioffe]] and [[Franklin Foer]] |date=2 October 2017 |work=[[The Atlantic]] |access-date=3 October 2017}}</ref>

=== Alleged involvement in Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections ===
{{main|Anastasia Vashukevich}}
In February 2018, [[Alexei Navalny]] published a video about a meeting between Deripaska and Deputy Prime Minister of Russia [[Sergei Eduardovich Prikhodko]] on a yacht traveling near Norway. According to Navalny, Deripaska probably served as a middle man between the Russian government represented by Prikhodko and Paul Manafort during [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections]].<ref name="Rybka"/> Prikhodko denied the allegations, accusing Navalny of "mixing the facts" about his "friend" Deripaska, [[Donald Trump]] and [[Paul Manafort]], while also voicing his wish to have talk with Navalny as a "man with a man".<ref name=":52">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rbc.ru/politics/09/02/2018/5a7dc6479a7947a4be81bebb|title=Вице-премьер Приходько заявил о желании ответить Навальному по-мужски|date=9 February 2018 |publisher=РБК|access-date=10 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|access-date=10 February 2018|work=Meduza|script-title=ru:Роскомнадзор потребовал от «Медиазоны» и «Радио Свобода» удалить фотографии из новости про Дерипаску, Приходько и Рыбку|url=https://meduza.io/news/2018/02/09/roskomnadzor-potreboval-ot-mediazony-udalit-fotografii-iz-novosti-pro-deripasku-prihodko-i-rybku|language=ru-RU}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|access-date=10 February 2018|title=Вице-премьер Приходько хочет ответить Навальному по-мужски|url=https://ura.news/news/1052323171}}</ref>

A day after the video was published, the [[Roskomnadzor]] added the video to the [[Federal List of Extremist Materials]], thus making accessing the video illegal for all Russian citizens.<ref>{{Cite news|access-date=10 February 2018|date=10 February 2018|work=Interfax.ru|script-title=ru:Суд включил в реестр запрещенной информации фильм ФБК о Дерипаске и Приходько|url=https://www.interfax.ru/russia/599352|language=ru-RU}}</ref> It also ordered [[YouTube]] to remove seven videos and [[Instagram]] to take down 14 points that were cited in the investigation; neither YouTube nor Instagram had responded as of 12 February 2018. According to a Roskomnadzor representative who spoke to ''[[Vedomosti]]'', a "court injunction of this sort against content hosted on Instagram and YouTube is unprecedented for Russia". The ''New York Times'' noted that this may presage a "more aggressive approach by the Russian government" to control online activities.<ref name="lux">{{cite news|last1=Luxmoore|first1=Matthew|title=Russia Threatens to Block YouTube and Instagram, After Complaints From an Oligarch|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/02/12/world/europe/russia-youtube-instagram-navalny.html|access-date=13 February 2018|work=New York Times|date=12 February 2018}}</ref>

In March 2018, fearing her own death while incarcerated in [[Bangkok]], [[Anastasia Vashukevich]], a Belarusian [[Escort agency|escort]] also known as Nastya Rybka who claimed to have over 16 hours of audio recordings she said could shed light on possible Russian interference in American elections.<ref name=DeripaskaGORDONua>{{cite news |last=ДВАЛИ |first=Наталия |url=https://english.gordonua.com/news/exclusiveenglish/former-kgb-agent-shvets-deripaska-supplied-to-ukraine-special-equipment-for-spying-on-us-embassy-and-diplomats-617515.html |title=Former KGB agent Shvets: Deripaska supplied to Ukraine special equipment for spying on U.S. embassy and diplomats |work=[[:uk:Гордон (інтернет-видання)|«ГОРДОН»]] (gordonua.com) |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=16 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240814215845/https://english.gordonua.com/news/exclusiveenglish/former-kgb-agent-shvets-deripaska-supplied-to-ukraine-special-equipment-for-spying-on-us-embassy-and-diplomats-617515.html |archive-date=14 August 2024}}</ref> She offered the recordings to American authorities in exchange for asylum, but was deported and arrested in a Russian airport. Vashukevich said the recordings from August 2016 include Deripaska discussing the United States presidential election with three English-speakers who Vashukevich believed were American. "Deripaska had a plan about elections", Vashukevich said. In court, Vashukevich apologized to Deripaska, and said Russian agents visited her in jail to urge her to cease public statements about him. ''The New York Times'' argued that her claims might be easily dismissed were it not for the Navalny video.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/05/world/asia/nastya-rybka-trump-putin.html|title=Escort Says Audio Recordings Show Russian Meddling in U.S. Election|first=Richard C.|last=Paddock|newspaper=The New York Times|date=5 March 2018|access-date=5 March 2018}}</ref> Deripaska denies an intimate history with Vashukevich.

=== Alleged child sex abuse ring involvement ===
According to {{ill|Verstka|ru|Вёрстка (издание)}} and [[iStories]], Deripaska was involved in a [[Child sex ring|child sexual abuse ring]] which was active from 2018 to 2019. The ring operated under the guise of regional [[beauty pageants]] for teenage girls across Russia. Journalists from these outlets alleged the sexual abuse took place in June 2019 in [[Krasnodar Krai]]. Following publication of the stories, Verstka and iStories experienced [[DDoS attacks]] on their Telegram channels.<ref>{{cite news |title=«Верстка» и «Важные истории»: миллиардер Дерипаска упоминается в уголовном деле о вовлечении несовершеннолетних в секс‑услуги как их клиент |trans-title="Verstka" and "Important Stories": Billionaire Deripaska is mentioned in a criminal case about involving minors in sex services as their client|url=https://zona.media/news/2025/06/19/deripaska |work=[[Mediazona]] |date=19 June 2025 |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Gerasimenko |first1=Olesya |last2=Zhadaev |first2=Ivan |last3=Richter |first3=Rina |last4=Kabanov |first4=Aleksandr |last5=Zholobova |first5=Maria |last6=Velikovsky |first6=Dmitry |title=“They Told Me: Deripaska Is the Client. Don't You Want To Sell Your Virginity?” |url=https://istories.media/en/stories/2025/06/19/they-told-me-deripaska-is-the-client-dont-you-want-to-sell-your-virginity/ |access-date=21 June 2025 |work=[[iStories]] |date=19 June 2025}}</ref>

== Sanctions ==
; Australian sanctions
On 18 March 2022, Australia added Deripaska to its sanctions list.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-03-18/oleg-deripaska-gladstone-alumina-refinery-australia-sanction/100920488 |title=Russian oligarchs with business interests in Australia sanctioned amid Ukraine war |last=Belot |first=Henry |website=ABC News |date=18 March 2022 |access-date=26 March 2022}}</ref>
; Canada sanctions
Deripaska was sanctioned by [[Canada]] under the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17), in relation to the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]], for Grave Breach of International Peace and Security.<ref>{{cite web |title=Special Economic Measures (Russia) Regulations (SOR/2014-58) |date=18 May 2023 |url=https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2014-58/page-4.html#docCont |access-date=24 June 2023}}</ref>

; European Union sanctions
On 8 April 2022, the EU added Deripaska to its sanctions list, freezing his assets and imposing a travel ban in all member states.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brussels |first=Shona Murray in |date=2022-04-08 |title=Rusal shareholder Oleg Deripaska sanctioned by EU |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/arid-40847762.html |access-date=2022-04-09 |website=Irish Examiner |language=en}}</ref> On 30 November 2022, Deripaska filed an appeal against the EU's decision to sanction him.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CURIA - Case information |url=https://curia.europa.eu/juris/fiche.jsf?id=T;732;22;RD;1;P;1;T2022/0732/P&nat=or&mat=or&pcs=Oor&jur=C,T,F&for=&jge=&dates=&language=en&pro=&cit=none%252CC%252CCJ%252CR%252C2008E%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252Ctrue%252Cfalse%252Cfalse&oqp=&td=;ALL&avg=&lgrec=en&parties=deripaska&lg=&cid=50167%22%20%5Cl%20%22topOfResultDiv |access-date=2023-02-17 |website=curia.europa.eu}}</ref>

Ukraine has claimed that assets belonging to Deripaska had been moved into the name of Siegfried Wolf, an Austrian citizen paid by Deripaska to avoid sanctions.<ref>{{cite web |title=Russian oligarch registers assets in name of Austrian national to avoid sanctions - watchdog |date=25 March 2023 |url=https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-economy/3687412-russian-oligarch-registers-assets-for-austrian-national-to-avoid-sanctions-watchdog.html |access-date=25 March 2023}}</ref>

; UK sanctions
Following the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], Deripaska was [[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War|sanctioned]] by the British government. This involved freezing his assets and a travel ban.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Prynn |first=Jonathan |date=10 March 2022 |title=Oleg Deripaska: Billionaire once named Russia's richest man added to sanctions list |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/uk/oleg-deripaska-billionaire-russian-oligarch-uk-sanctions-list-b987301.html |access-date=10 March 2022 |website=[[Evening Standard]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=CONSOLIDATED LIST OF FINANCIAL SANCTIONS TARGETS IN THE UK |url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1150217/Russia.pdf |access-date=16 April 2023}}</ref>

Deripaska-linked UK company Terra Services Ltd. was raided in December 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-10-18/deripaska-linked-firm-was-raided-for-undisclosed-u-s-inquiry |title=Oleg Deripaska-Linked Firm Was Raided for Undisclosed U.S. Inquiry |author=Jonathan Browning |date=18 October 2019 |website=bloomberg.com |access-date=20 October 2019}}</ref>

; U.S. sanctions
{{See also|Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act}}
In April 2018, the United States imposed sanctions on Deripaska and 23 other Russian tycoons and officials.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.treasury.gov/resource-center/sanctions/OFAC-Enforcement/Pages/20180406.aspx |title=Ukraine-/Russia-related Designations and Identification Update|date=6 April 2018 |website=[[United States Department of the Treasury]] |access-date=6 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://meduza.io/news/2018/04/06/ssha-vveli-sanktsii-protiv-36-rossiyskih-biznesmenov |script-title=ru:США ввели санкции против семи российских олигархов и 17 чиновников из «кремлевского списка» |trans-title=The US imposed sanctions against seven Russian oligarchs and 17 officials from the "Kremlin list" |date=6 April 2018 |website=[[Meduza (website)|Meduza]] |access-date=6 April 2018 |language=ru}}</ref> The statement of the [[United States Department of the Treasury]] said that Deripaska "ha[d] been accused of threatening the lives of business rivals, illegally wiretapping a government official, and taking part in extortion and racketeering".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sm0338 |title=Treasury Designates Russian Oligarchs, Officials, and Entities in Response to Worldwide Malign Activity|date=6 April 2018 |website=[[United States Department of the Treasury]] |access-date=11 April 2018}}</ref>

In May 2018, it was reported that Deripaska had to return three private jets owned by [[Credit Suisse]] and [[Raiffeisen (Switzerland)|Raiffeisen]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-05-10 |title=Exclusive: Sanctioned Russian tycoon hands back his private jets |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-sanctions-russia-rusal-jets-exclu-idUSKBN1IB2JR |access-date=2023-03-20}}</ref>

In October 2018 the U.S. Treasury announced that it had extended until 12 December a deadline for the full imposition of sanctions against Rusal and its parent company [[En+ Group]], pending the review of the proposals presented by En+ Group to the U.S. government that would see Deripaska reduce his stake in En+ to below 45 per cent from around 70 per cent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/2616733e-ce27-11e8-9fe5-24ad351828ab|title=US delays start date for sanctions on Deripaska's Rusal|newspaper=Financial Times|language=en-GB|date=12 October 2018}}</ref>

In January 2019 the U.S. Treasury lifted the sanctions on companies formerly controlled by Deripaska. Sanctions on Deripaska himself remained in effect.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/01/27/u-s-lifts-sanctions-on-rusal-other-firms-linked-to-russias-deripaska.html|title=U.S. lifts sanctions on firms linked to Russia's Deripaska|website=CNBC|date=27 January 2019|access-date=1 February 2019|archive-date=1 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401093634/https://www.cnbc.com/2019/01/27/u-s-lifts-sanctions-on-rusal-other-firms-linked-to-russias-deripaska.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In April 2019, the U.S. Treasury Department nonetheless allowed Deripaska to transfer 10.5 million shares of his holding company En+ Group to a trust fund for his children as part of a divorce settlement with his ex-wife Polina Yumasheva, which had been finalized before the sanctions were put in place.<ref name=NYT>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/08/us/politics/sanctions-deripaska.html |title=Sanctions Deal With Russian Oligarch Included Transfer of Shares to Benefit His Children |newspaper=New York Times |author1=Kenneth P. Vogel |author2=Andrew E Kramer |date=8 April 2019}}</ref> The deal to have U.S. sanctions removed from En+ Group was brokered by [[Greg Barker, Baron Barker of Battle|Greg Barker]], a UK legislator, who in February 2019 went on to be appointed chairman of En+ Group.<ref name="ukwhore4">{{cite news|url=https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/british-lord-barker-got-4-million-bonus-on-deripaska-sanctions-deal-1.1252584|title=British Lord Barker Got $4 Million Bonus on Deripaska Sanctions Deal|agency=Bloomberg|date=2 May 2019}}</ref><ref name="barkerleaves">{{cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/greg-barker-leaves-lords-to-run-oligarch-oleg-deripaskas-metals-empire-km7gclptf|title=Greg Barker leaves Lords to run oligarch Oleg Deripaska's metals empire|newspaper=The Times (UK)|date=24 February 2019}}</ref>

In March 2019, Deripaska sued the United States, alleging that it had overstepped its legal bounds in imposing sanctions on him and made him the "latest victim" in the FBI probe into Russia's interference in U.S. elections.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Susan |first1=Heavey |last2=Nathan |first2=Layne |title=Russian metals tycoon Deripaska sues U.S. over sanctions |url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-usa-russia-deripaska/russian-metals-tycoon-deripaska-sues-u-s-over-sanctions-idUKKCN1QW2PQ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190315200348/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-usa-russia-deripaska/russian-metals-tycoon-deripaska-sues-u-s-over-sanctions-idUKKCN1QW2PQ |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 March 2019 |date=15 March 2019}}</ref> U.S. District Court Judge [[Amit Mehta]] dismissed the suit in June 2021, ruling it lacked merit.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/us-judge-dismisses-russian-tycoon-deripaskas-lawsuit-against-us-filing-2021-06-14/|title=U.S. judge dismisses Russian tycoon Deripaska's lawsuit against U.S. -filing|newspaper=Reuters|date=14 June 2021|via=www.reuters.com}}</ref> On 3 October 2022, the US Supreme Court rejected the oligarch's appeal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.banki.ru/news/lenta/?id=10973204|title=Верховный суд США отклонил ходатайство Дерипаски об отмене санкций|language=ru|date=2022-10-03|website=banki.ru}}</ref>

On 29 September 2022 the [[United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York]] accused Deripaska of sanctions evasion. According to the prosecutor's office, Deripaska, through Gracetown Inc., illegally used the U.S. financial system to service real estate objects owned by him. In this he was assisted by two women: Olga Shriki, who operated in the United States, and Natalia Bardakova, who directed Shriki from Russia. They are also charged with violating U.S. sanctions. Chriqui was arrested on 29 September. All three "are charged with one count of conspiring to violate and evade U.S. sanctions, in violation of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison," the statement says.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/russian-oligarch-oleg-vladimirovich-deripaska-and-associates-indicted-sanctions-evasion|title=Russian Oligarch Oleg Vladimirovich Deripaska And Associates Indicted For Sanctions Evasion And Obstruction Of Justice|date=2022-09-29|website=justice.gov}}</ref> Graham Bonham-Carter has been charged with helping Deripaska evade sanctions.<ref>[https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-63218643 UK businessman charged with 'helping Russian oligarch evade sanctions']</ref>

In January 2023, [[Charles McGonigal]], a former head of counterintelligence in the FBI New York City field office, was charged with conspiring with co-defendant Sergey Shestakov, a former Soviet and Russian diplomat who is a U.S. citizen, to provide services to Deripaska in 2021, in violation of U.S. sanctions imposed on Deripaska in 2018. They allegedly did so by investigating a rival Russian oligarch in return for concealed payments from Deripaska, using shell companies in the contract that outlined the services to be performed, using a forged signature on that contract, and using the same shell companies to send and receive payment from Deripaska.<ref>[https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/former-special-agent-charge-fbi-new-york-counterintelligence-division-charged-violating-us Former Special Agent in Charge of the FBI New York Counterintelligence Division Charged with Violating U.S. Sanctions on Russia],''[[United States Department of Justice]]'', January 23, 2023. Retrieved January 23, 2023.</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/23/nyregion/fbi-money-laundering-charles-mcgonigal.html Former Top F.B.I. Official in New York Charged With Aiding Oligarch], ''[[New York Times]]'', Benjamin Weiser and William K. Rashbaum, January 23, 2023. Retrieved January 23, 2023.</ref>

== Personal life ==
Deripaska was married to Polina Yumasheva, the daughter of [[Boris Yeltsin]]'s top adviser [[Valentin Yumashev]] and stepdaughter of Yeltsin's daughter [[Tatyana Yumasheva|Tatyana]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Godzimirski |first=Jakub M. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Zm0tDwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Polina+Yumasheva%22&pg=PA221 |title=The Political Economy of Russian Aluminium: Between the Dual State and Global Markets |date=2017-07-18 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-57234-5 |language=en}}</ref> While Yeltsin was president, Deripaska's close ties put him in Yeltsin's inner circle, dubbed "The Family".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/08/20/business/yourmoney/20oligarch.html|title=Out of Siberia, a Russian Way to Wealth|last=Kramer|first=Andrew E.|date=20 August 2006|work=The New York Times|access-date=2 June 2017|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/7063201/Boris-Yeltsins-daughter-attacks-Vladimir-Putin.html|title=Boris Yeltsin's daughter attacks Vladimir Putin|last=Osborn|first=Andrew|work=Telegraph.co.uk|access-date=2 June 2017|language=en}}</ref> Deripaska and Yumasheva were married from 2001 to 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-10 |title=Oleg Deripaska: Putin 'favourite' with strong ties to Britain |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/mar/10/oleg-deripaska-profile-putin-britain |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Vogel |first1=Kenneth P. |last2=Kramer |first2=Andrew E. |date=2019-04-08 |title=Sanctions Deal With Russian Oligarch Included Transfer of Shares to Benefit His Children |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/08/us/politics/sanctions-deripaska.html |access-date=2022-04-06 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite news |script-title=ru:Жёны известных людей зарабатывают на ресторанах и галереях |language=ru-RU |work=Рамблер/новости |url=https://news.rambler.ru/other/40543183-zheny-izvestnyh-lyudey-zarabatyvayut-na-restoranah-i-galereyah/ |url-status=dead |access-date=15 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815164532/https://news.rambler.ru/other/40543183-zheny-izvestnyh-lyudey-zarabatyvayut-na-restoranah-i-galereyah/ |archive-date=15 August 2018}}</ref> The Deripaskas have two children: a son, Pyotr (born 2001), and daughter, Maria (born 2003).<ref>{{cite news|script-title=ru:Блоги / Эхо-рейтинг: Полина Дерипаска| url=http://echo.msk.ru/blog/echo_rating/850130-echo/|access-date=25 May 2017|work=Echo Moscow|language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|script-title=ru:Президент "Русал" Олег Дерипаска. Биография|url=https://ria.ru/spravka/20141118/1033854288.html|access-date=25 May 2017|work=RIA Novosti|date=18 November 2014|language=ru}}</ref> Deripaska practices yoga, swimming, horseback riding, and hiking. At his home near Moscow, he has seven horses and six dogs.<ref name=":0"/>

In March 2018, it was reported that Deripaska had successfully acquired [[Cypriot citizenship]] in 2017, under [[Cyprus|that country's]] [[golden visa]] rule, which generates billions{{clarify|date=April 2023}} in revenue for the island nation. According to documents seen by ''[[The Guardian]]'', Deripaska's first attempt to become a citizen of a country in the EU was unsuccessful because of a preliminary inquiry into his activities in Belgium. This inquiry was dismissed in 2016.<ref name="guardian02032018"/>

In 2009, Deripaska's ranking fell to No. 164, with ''Forbes'' stating: "[H]e may not withstand collapsing markets and heavy debts".<ref name="Fo03">{{cite news| url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/2009/10/billionaires-2009-richest-people_Oleg-Deripaska_UCP9.html |work=Forbes |title=#164 Oleg Deripaska – The World's Billionaires 2009 |date=11 March 2009}}</ref>

In 2010, his estimated $US10.7 billion fortune allowed him to rise to No. 57 of the World's Billionaires list.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/2010/10/billionaires-2010_Oleg-Deripaska_UCP9.html |title=The World's Billionaires 2010, Forbes |work=Forbes |date=12 February 2010 |access-date=14 May 2011}}</ref> According to ''Forbes'' magazine, he removed the heads of his two largest companies and personally negotiated with the Russian government, banks, and other creditors to restructure his loan obligations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/oleg-deripaska/|title=Oleg Deripaska|website=Forbes}}</ref> Deripaska himself in 2007 was reported to have consistently said that the estimate of his wealth was exaggerated, that it did not completely account for the amount of debt he incurred, and that he should be ranked far below the top ten on the list of the Russian billionaires.<ref name="guardian.co.uk">{{cite news|title=How metals and a ruthless streak put Russian patriot at top of the rich list |first=Luke |last=Harding |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2007/feb/24/business.russia |work=The Guardian |location=UK |access-date=14 May 2011 |date=24 February 2007}}</ref>

''Forbes'' estimated his fortune at $US3.3&nbsp;billion in 2015,<ref name=Fo01>{{cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/oleg-deripaska/|work=[[Forbes]]|last=Rapoza|title=Forbes Profile: Oleg Deripaska|access-date=25 June 2021}}</ref> $5.2 billion in 2017,<ref name="forbes">{{Cite news |title=Oleg Deripaska |work=[[Forbes]] |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/oleg-deripaska/ |access-date=27 July 2019}}</ref> $3.3 billion in 2019,<ref name="forbes" /> $3.8 billion in 2021,<ref name="forbes" /> $2.5 billion in 2023,<ref name="forbes" /> In July 2025, ''Forbes'' estimated his net worth to be $US4.1 billion.<ref name=":9" />

Deripaska's Cypriot−registered company Edenfield Investments acquired the Grade II listed [[Hamstone House]] in the [[St George's Hill]] district of Weybridge, Surrey, in 2001.<ref>{{cite news|title=Son of Putin ally has £35m London house |last1=Boswell |first1=Josh |last2=Hollingsworth |first2=Mark |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/son-of-putin-ally-has-35m-london-homehouse-list-reveals-mansions-of-the-oligarchs-8dzrtnxk6 |access-date=17 March 2019 |work=[[The Times]] |date=20 March 2016 |page=10}}</ref> Since 2006, Deripaska has owned the [[Herbert Haft|Haft mansion]] near [[Embassy Row]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], through a company incorporated in Delaware.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/the-russian-tycoon-next-door-putin-ally-is-tied-to-one-of-dcs-swankiest-mansions/2017/11/28/15f913de-cef6-11e7-81bc-c55a220c8cbe_story.html |title=The Russian billionaire next door: Putin ally is tied to one of D.C.'s swankiest mansions |author1=Rosalind S. Helderman |author2=Alice Crites |date=29 November 2017 |newspaper=Washington Post |access-date=4 December 2017}}</ref>

He owns a mansion in [[Belgravia]].<ref name="Ravellot">{{cite news|title=Ukraine: Squatters occupy Russian oligarch's London mansion|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-60736583|access-date=14 March 2022|work=BBC|archive-date=14 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220314121744/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-60736583}}</ref><ref name="OccupiedMansion">{{cite news|title=Squatters occupy London mansion 'owned by Russian oligarch' in protest at Ukraine war|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/russian-oligarch-mansion-squatters-london-b2035179.html|access-date=14 March 2022|work=The Independent|archive-date=14 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220314121752/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/russian-oligarch-mansion-squatters-london-b2035179.html}}</ref>

===Charitable and other activities===
Oleg Deripaska sits on the board of trustees of the [[Bolshoi Theatre]], and has financed [[ballet]] performances like ''[[Flames of Paris]]'', ''[[La Sylphide]]'', and ''[[Paquita]]'' as well as [[opera]]s like ''[[The Legend of the Invisible City of Kitezh and the Maiden Fevroniya]]'', ''[[Carmen]]'', and ''[[Wozzeck]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.ru/profile/oleg-deripaska|title=Олег Дерипаска|work=Forbes Russia|date=15 April 2011|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref>

In 1998, Deripaska established a charitable foundation in Russia, Volnoe Delo.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.europeanceo.com/profiles/oleg-deripaska-and-the-russian-aluminium-wars/|title=Oleg Deripaska and the Russian aluminium wars|access-date=25 May 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://volnoe-delo.ru/en/|title=Volnoe Delo Foundation|website=volnoe-delo.ru|language=ru|access-date=25 May 2018}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://volnoe-delo.ru/|title=Фонд "Вольное Дело"|website=volnoe-delo.ru}}</ref> The fund supports initiatives in Russia aimed at developing education and science, preserving spiritual and cultural heritage, and improving standards in public health.<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heritagedaily.com/2016/08/darius-i-stele-found-in-ancient-town-of-phanagoria-in-russia/112378|title=Darius I stele found in ancient town of Phanagoria in Russia - HeritageDaily - Heritage & Archaeology News|website=heritagedaily.com|date=9 August 2016|language=en-US|access-date=25 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/billionaire-sochi-stray-dogs_n_4767912?guccounter=1|title=Billionaire Saves Sochi Stray Dogs!|date=11 February 2014|work=HuffPost UK|access-date=25 May 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref> Since 1998, Deripaska claims to have invested in more than 500 charity programs in 50 regions of Russia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://volnoe-delo.ru/en/|title=Volnoe Delo Foundation|website=volnoe-delo.ru|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref>{{additional citation needed|date=February 2018}} Volnoe Delo has supported research activities in the 2,550-year-old city of [[Phanagoria]] since 2004. More than $10 million has been allocated to Phanagoria fieldwork over the past 14 years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://popular-archaeology.com/article/darius-i-stele-found-in-ancient-town-of-phanagoria-in-russia/|title=Popular Archeology - Darius I stele found in ancient town of Phanagoria in Russia|work=Popular Archeology|access-date=25 May 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Today, Phanagoria is one of the best-equipped archeological sites in Russia and has a scientific and cultural center, equipment and technology for above-ground and underwater excavation, as well as a team of specialists involved in the excavation process.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://popular-archaeology.com/issue/06052014/article/ancient-naval-ram-found-in-phanagoria-reveals-history-of-popular-unrest-in-63-b-c|title=Ancient naval ram found in Phanagoria reveals history of popular unrest in 63 B.C.|work=Popular Archeology|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> In 2014, Volnoe Delo foundation launched a programme for students' early career guidance and professional training—JuniorSkills.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://volnoe-delo.ru/en/events/news/junior-skills/|title=Junior Skills|website=volnoe-delo.ru|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> The first, pilot, championship on professional skills, JuniorSkills Hi-Tech, was held in the Urals city of [[Yekaterinburg]] in 2014, part of the nationwide championship on cross-industry blue-collar professions in high-tech "WorldSkills". In 2020 during the pandemic of COVID-19 it bought new ambulances and sent them to twelve Russian towns in [[Siberia]] and [[Ural Mountains|the Urals]].<ref name="intellinews.com">{{Cite web|date=20 April 2020|title=Deripaska steps up to Russia's fight against the coronavirus pandemic|url=https://www.intellinews.com/deripaska-steps-up-to-russia-s-fight-against-the-coronavirus-pandemic-181365/|access-date=18 February 2021|website=www.intellinews.com|language=en}}</ref>

Deripaska was a member of the International Council at [[Harvard University]]'s [[Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfercenter.org/person/oleg-deripaska|title=Oleg Deripaska|publisher=Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs|access-date=4 May 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405171539/https://www.belfercenter.org/person/oleg-deripaska|archive-date=5 April 2017}}</ref>

In 2017, during the [[Responses to the West African Ebola virus epidemic|West African Ebola virus epidemic]] Deripaska personally initiated construction of the Centre for Epidemic and Microbiological Research and Treatment in the Guinean [[Kindia Region|Kindia]] province. The centre was designed and constructed by [[United Company RUSAL|RUSAL]] specialists with the assistance of [[Rospotrebnadzor]] scientists (RUSAL has invested $10 million).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://africatimes.com/2017/05/22/ebola-2-0-lessons-learned-in-2014-may-not-suffice/|title=Ebola 2.0 – Lessons Learned in 2014 May Not Suffice|date=22 May 2017|website=Africa Times|access-date=25 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170523055530/http://africatimes.com/2017/05/22/ebola-2-0-lessons-learned-in-2014-may-not-suffice/|archive-date=23 May 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In February 2014, Deripaska financed the construction of makeshift kennels to house stray dogs that had been abandoned by construction workers after completing work on the [[Sochi Olympic Stadium|Sochi Olympic Village]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/sochi-olympic-parks-condemned-stray-dogs-saved-by-russian-billionaire-9118727.html|title=Sochi Olympic Park's condemned stray dogs 'saved by Russian billionaire'|last=Withnall|first=Adam|date=10 February 2014|work=[[The Independent]]|access-date=10 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140211211903/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/sochi-olympic-parks-condemned-stray-dogs-saved-by-russian-billionaire-9118727.html|archive-date=11 February 2014|url-status=dead|location=London}}</ref>

In October 2015 Deripaska called for governments not to agree to the Paris climate accords since they lacked legally-binding mechanisms and arguing that countries like India and China needed to contribute more to avoid competition problems.<ref name=":11">{{Cite news |last1=Sanderson |first1=Henry |last2=Clark |first2=Pilita |date=18 October 2015 |title=Deripaska warns about competitive risks from Paris climate deal |work=Financial Times |url=http://www.ft.com/intl/cms/s/0/b72f19fe-7432-11e5-a129-3fcc4f641d98.html |access-date=13 January 2016 |issn=0307-1766}}</ref>

In 2020, during the pandemic he donated money to construct hospitals in Siberia.<ref name="intellinews.com" />

As part of a public relations campaign, he said in April 2021 that [[Rosstat]] (Federal State Statistics Service) data showing that there are 17.8 million poor people living below the country's subsistence minimum was wrong, and that the correct number was about 80 million.<ref name=rosstat>{{Cite web |title=Дерипаска обвинил Росстат в "жонглировании цифрами" о числе бедных |url=https://www.rbc.ru/society/19/04/2021/607d261c9a79479bb67890a9 |access-date=27 November 2021 |website=РБК |date=19 April 2021 |language=ru}}</ref>

Deripaska criticized the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]] on several occasions.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|title=Two Russian oligarchs call for an end to Putin's war |last=Riley |first=Charles |date=28 February 2022 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/02/28/business/oligarchs-russia-ukraine-fridman-deripaska/index.html |website=CNN |access-date=16 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |agency=[[Agence France Presse]] |date=28 February 2022 |title=Russian tycoon Deripaska says time to end 'state capitalism' in Russia |url=https://editor.guardian.ng/news/russian-tycoon-deripaska-says-time-to-end-state-capitalism-in-russia/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|newspaper=[[The Guardian (Nigeria)|The Guardian]]|language=en-US |access-date=16 March 2022}}</ref><ref name="odtmt">{{cite news |title=Russian Oligarch Deripaska Says Destroying Ukraine Would Be 'Colossal Mistake' |url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2022/06/28/russian-oligarch-deripaska-says-destroying-ukraine-would-be-colossal-mistake-a78132 |agency=AFP |publisher=The Moscow Times |date=28 June 2022}}</ref> On 20 December 2022, a Russian court had ordered the seizure of a luxury hotel complex in Sochi worth $1 billion owned by Deripaska. The seizure might be triggered by Deripaska's criticism of the war.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-12-20 |title=Billionaire Oleg Deripaska's Sochi hotel complex seized after Russian court order |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/32052a11-89f3-4642-8dd4-11433a32f8a2 |access-date=2023-02-16}}</ref>

He sits on the board of trustees of the School of Business Administration, the School of Public Administration, and the School of Economics at [[Moscow State University]] as well as the School of Business Administration at [[St. Petersburg State University]].{{citation needed|date=February 2024}} Deripaska is a co-founder of the National Science Support Foundation and the National Medicine Fund.{{citation needed|date=February 2024}} In 1999, he was awarded the [[Order of Friendship]], a state award of the [[Russian Federation]].{{citation needed|date=February 2024}}
